findings.title: Salesforce refresh path references an unimported Prisma client
findings.body: The newly added refresh path calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this file does not import `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. Type-checking will fail with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`; if type-checking is skipped during deployment, every Salesforce refresh reaching this line throws a `ReferenceError`.

findings.title: Google refresh persists the Zod SafeParse wrapper instead of credential data
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a successful `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed token object. This line saves that wrapper as `Credential.key`, whereas `googleCredentialSchema` expects token fields such as `access_token` at the top level. After the first refresh, subsequent Google Calendar service instances cannot parse the persisted credential and the integration stops working.

findings.title: The minimum sync-response schema does not preserve or validate expiry fields
findings.body: The computed properties here are not Zod index signatures: both `z.string().toString()` expressions become the literal key `"[object Object]"`, with the second overwriting the first. Zod therefore accepts only `access_token` and strips normal unknown fields such as `expires_in` and `expiry_date`. When sync is enabled, a source endpoint's expiry value is discarded, causing adapters to save an already-expired or invalid token state and repeatedly refresh or fail.

findings.title: Missing refresh tokens are replaced with a fake value and can corrupt saved credentials
findings.body: The documented sync endpoint response contains only an access token and expiry, so this branch commonly injects the literal string `"refresh_token"`. Callers such as Zoom and Office then merge or assign that value into the stored credential, overwriting the real provider refresh token. If sync is later disabled or unavailable, direct provider refreshes will use the fake token and the user must reconnect the integration.

findings.title: Sync refresh responses are returned as raw fetch Responses despite incompatible caller contracts
findings.body: The sync branch returns the native `fetch` `Response`, while the original refresh functions return provider-specific objects. Existing callers are not normalized for this: Google reads `res.data`, HubSpot treats the result as a `HubspotToken`, and the Zoho adapters expect an Axios response with `.data`. A JSON response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` therefore yields undefined token fields or invalid persisted credentials for these integrations instead of a successful source-of-truth refresh.

findings.title: Credential-sync token requests contain no authentication
findings.body: The request to the configured credential source sends only a predictable numeric `calcomUserId` and an app slug. It includes neither `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, the configured header name, nor any signature or other credential. A source endpoint cannot authenticate this request using the supplied sync configuration, so anyone able to reach that endpoint can forge requests for user IDs and potentially obtain their current third-party access tokens. The request needs an authenticated header/signature and the receiver must verify it.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends a credential ID as the remote Cal.com user ID
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects its third argument to be the credential owner's user ID and serializes it as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`. Credential IDs and user IDs are unrelated; normal sync requests will fail to locate the owner, and an ID that happens to match another user can fetch that user's source credential and save its access token onto the current user's credential.

findings.title: Zoom refresh uses a non-existent app slug for credential sync
findings.body: The helper parameter is an app slug, but this call sends `zoomvideo`. The same integration creates credentials with app ID `zoom` and uses `zoom` as its installed-app slug. A source endpoint that keys credentials by the documented app slug will not find Zoom credentials, so Zoom sync refreshes fail.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint
findings.body: Unlike the other modified refresh paths, Salesforce always posts directly to Salesforce's token endpoint and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`. Consequently, enabling `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no effect for Salesforce: Cal.com continues to use its local refresh token rather than the self-hosted app store designated as the source of truth.

findings.title: Concurrent webhook deliveries can create duplicate credentials
findings.body: The lookup and create are separate operations with no transaction, uniqueness constraint, or idempotency key. Two simultaneous deliveries for a user/app with no existing credential can both observe no row and both create one. Later syncs update an arbitrary `findFirst` result, while calendar code may select a different duplicate, leaving stale credentials active and making the integration behavior nondeterministic.
